Team — looping you all in on a concise proposal for the next two weeks of evidence work for the EU/AZ regional audits. I put together an initial control-mapping heatmap that attempts to prioritize what we should surface first to the assessors. Please see the attached spreadsheet (control-mapping-heatmap.xlsx).

Quick background: QuantumBank has requested an accelerated sampling window for their SOC/SIG intake, and Acadia will be doing the FedRAMP-style controls crosswalk for a subset of services. We need to confirm:

- control owners for the top 30 controls in the heatmap
- acceptable redaction guidance for screenshots/logs (customer asked explicitly)
- sample extraction windows (preferred date ranges)

Asks:
- Kimberly: can you populate the "owner" and "evidence location" columns in the sheet by EOD Friday?
- Rishi: please confirm whether we can provide KMS key rotation artifacts and whether they need HSM-level attestations for this engagement.
- Marissa: can you coordinate with Julia on the QuantumBank side about acceptable redaction for PII?

Attached: control-mapping-heatmap.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — Sofia

Subject: Re: Control mapping heatmap & pre-audit evidence triage (EU/AZ region)

Thanks — received and useful. A few notes from the assessor side:

- Redaction: screenshots with PII redacted are fine; hashes/IDs are preferred in a separate CSV so we can map back to samples without needing raw PII.
- KMS/HSM: redacted HSM serials + signed attestation PDF are acceptable for FedRAMP-style artifacts. If you can produce a short narrative (1 paragraph) about key custody and rotation cadence, that expedites review.
- Sampling windows: we need two non-overlapping 14-day windows in Q3 to validate operational controls. Please confirm exact ranges by 18 Sep 18:00 UTC.

Preferred intake: a single Drive folder, with a folder per control and a short manifest (manifest.csv) describing file types and redaction status.

We can accept a zipped bundle for initial dry-run; please label artifacts with the control id from the heatmap.

-Liam O'Connor
Senior Assessor
Acadia Security
